text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The head of the Latvian delegation to the Baltic Assembly, Ivars Kezbers doubts that the Baltic States will be invited to join the EU until the year 2000 and NATO during the first stage of its expansion eastwards. On his return from the assmbly's meeting in the Estonian town of Parnu, Kezbers said the Baltics should elaborate a common stance in their foreign, defence and security policies.
- The lists of candidates for the local elections due on March 9 are to be submitted to the central election commission starting on January 18-29.
- Romualdas Razukas, former leader of the Latvian Popular Front in 1990-1992, has decided to return to politics by joining the centrist Latvia's Way party.

- A rehabilitation centre for children having suffered from sexual abuse has been opened in Bulduri, the first of the kind in Latvia. According to the Latvian branch of "Save the Children", there are at least 15 such children in Latvia.
- Ventspils Nafta is to provide its regular tariff discounts of five to 20 percent to its major partners - intermediaries, representing the major Russian oil companies.

- President Guntis Ulmanis plans to visit a number of foreign capitals during the first half of the year, he said in a radio interview. His destinations include Turkey, France, Denmark and Poland, with the main topics being security and the role of the Baltic States in a united Europe.
